resources.string: Google only shares the stops, not the road: for now they are joined with straight lines. The real road comes with route planning.
In Google Maps, build the route with its stops, tap Share and copy the link. Then paste it here.
Unknown format. GPX or KML files and Google Maps links work.
The GPX file has no track and fewer than two stops.
The KML file has no line and fewer than two points.
This is not a Google Maps link.
No stops found in the Google Maps link.
The link has a single place: a route needs at least a start and a finish.
The Google Maps link has stops without coordinates (e.g. “Your location”). Pick exact places and share again.
The link uses names without coordinates: open it in Google Maps and share it again from there.
The file is too big (over 30 MB).
The compressed file contains neither a KML nor a GPX.
The Google link does not lead to a route.
The Google link goes through too many steps: open it in Google Maps and share it again.
No connection: opening a short Google link needs the internet.
It is downloaded from the project’s Releases page and Android asks you to confirm.
In the settings, turn on “Allow from this source” for RidePlan, then come back and tap Update again.
Confirm in the Android window. Then reopen RidePlan.
The downloaded file does not match the published one. It was not installed.
The installed version is signed differently (e.g. a test build). Uninstall it and install the APK from the Releases page by hand.
